{{short description|German mathematician}}
'''Walter Trump''' (born 1953<ref>Andreas Stiller: [https://www.heise.de/ct/artikel/Der-Wuerfel-ist-gefallen-289094.html ''Der Würfel ist gefallen. Kleinster perfekter magischer Würfel gefunden'']. heise.de, 1 December 2003 (German) </ref>) is a [[Germany|German]] [[mathematician]] from Bavaria and a retired high school teacher. He is known for his work in [[recreational mathematics]].

He has made contributions working on both the [[square packing in a square|square packing problem]] and the magic tile problem. In 1979 he discovered the optimal known packing of 11 equal squares in a larger square,<ref>{{cite book |title=Which way did the bicycle go?: and other intriguing mathematical mysteries |last=Konhauser |first=Joseph D. E. |author2=Daniel J. Velleman |author3=S. Wagon |page=[https://archive.org/details/whichwaydidbicyc0000konh/page/105 105] |year=1996 |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-0-88385-325-2 |url=https://archive.org/details/whichwaydidbicyc0000konh/page/105 }}</ref> and in 2003, along with [[Christian Boyer]], developed the first known [[magic cube]] of order 5.<ref>{{cite book |title=Number freak: from 1 to 200— the hidden language of numbers revealed |author-link=Derrick Niederman |last=Niederman |first=Derrick |page=63 |year=2009 |publisher=[[Penguin Books|Penguin]] |isbn=978-0-399-53459-1 }}</ref> In 2012, Trump&nbsp;''et al.'' described a model for retention of liquid on random surfaces.<ref name="Knecht11">{{cite journal
  | last = Knecht
  | first = Craig
  |author2=Walter Trump |author3=Daniel ben-Avraham |author4=Robert M. Ziff
   | title = Retention capacity of random surfaces
  | journal =  Physical Review Letters
  | volume = 108
  | issue = 4
  | year = 2012
  | article-number = 045703
  | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.108.045703| arxiv =1110.6166| bibcode =2012PhRvL.108d5703K | pmid=22400865}}
</ref>
In 2014, he and [[Francis Gaspalou]] were able to calculate all 8 × 8 [[Multimagic square#Bimagic square|bimagic squares]].<ref name="W. Trump">[http://www.trump.de/magic-squares/ Notes on Magic Squares and Cubes] by Walter Trump</ref>

Until he retired in 2015,<ref>[https://orcid.org/0000-0001-6011-7233 Trump Walter (0000-0001-6011-7233) - ORCID]</ref> Trump worked as a teacher for mathematics and physics at the [[Gymnasium (school)|Gymnasium]] in [[Stein, Bavaria]].
